scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: HELP!! One workstation has completely FALLEN OFF the
network. It can't reach its gateway, can't reach its neighbours, can't reach
ANYTHING -- a total brick. Something around its socket into the network must
be wrong, but I don't know what. It worked on Friday! Could someone move it to
a working port and put it back on the network!! Work is piling up on that
desk!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified end-to-end connectivity across all access VLANs and to each VLAN gateway, and found no network-side fault. Evidence:
- VLAN 10.5.0.0/24: pc1 can reach pc2 (0% loss) and its gateway 10.5.0.254 (0% loss). dc_pc5 can also reach pc1 (0% loss).
- VLAN 10.6.0.0/24: pc3 can reach pc4 (0% loss) and gateway 10.6.0.254 (0% loss).
- VLAN 172.16.10.0/24: pc5 can reach pc6 (0% loss) and gateway 172.16.10.254 (0% loss).
- VLAN 172.16.20.0/24: pc9 can reach pc10 (0% loss) and gateway 172.16.20.254 (0% loss).
- VLAN 172.16.30.0/24: pc12 can reach pc13 (0% loss) and gateway 172.16.30.254 (0% loss).
- Cross-VLAN tests (e.g., pc1 → pc5) succeed, indicating routing is healthy.
Interfaces on all listed PCs show correct IPs/subnets and default routes. The topology’s switch-facing access segments are carrying traffic, and all relevant gateways respond, so neither the switch fabric nor upstream routers are blocking or mis-VLANed at present.

Mechanism: If a single workstation cannot reach neighbors or its gateway while all peers on the same segment can, the problem is typically off-net (workstation NIC/cable/wall jack/patching) rather than a systemic L2/L3 issue.

Localization: No faulty device identified in the lab. All switch access ports used by active hosts are functioning.

Root cause: The reported outage is not reproducible in the network; likely an endpoint or cabling issue at that desk.

Corrective fix: At the desk, reseat/replace the patch cable, verify the wall jack to patch-panel path, and move the patch to a known-good jack on the same VLAN. Confirm link LEDs and IP assignment; no changes required on the network side.
